claims.text: Premier's statement on declaration of state of provincial emergency (8 August 2026): BC's Minister of Emergency Management and Climate Readiness, Kelly Greene, declared a State of Provincial Emergency, citing 'the addition of this new, fast-moving fire and the large-scale evacuation that occurred overnight' near Summerland (the Bald Range fire), stating emergency officials 'now need the specific tools it enables available.'

As of 15 August 2026, EmergencyInfoBC lists active wildfire evacuation orders/alerts for the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen, City of Revelstoke, Regional District of North Okanagan, Okanagan Indian Band, Cayoose Creek Indian Band, Village of Clinton and Thompson-Nicola Regional District.

EmergencyInfoBC provincial emergencies listing (checked 17 August 2026): confirms the State of Provincial Emergency declared 8 August 2026 is still in effect, with active wildfire evacuation orders/alerts listed for the Regional District of North Okanagan, Okanagan Indian Band, Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen, District of Summerland, City of Revelstoke and other regional districts and First Nations, most recently updated 16 August 2026.

GDACS wildfire report for Canada (event id 1030240, episode 37, reporting window 08 Aug 2026 - 16 Aug 2026): burned area 25,829 hectares (up from 25,391 ha in episode 31); affected population 4,912 people in the burned area (unchanged from episode 31).

GDACS wildfire report for Canada (event id 1030240, episode 39, reporting window 08 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC - 17 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC): burned area 26,618 hectares (up from 25,829 ha in episode 37); affected population 4,912 people in the burned area (unchanged from episode 37).

EmergencyInfoBC provincial emergencies listing (checked 18 August 2026): confirms the State of Provincial Emergency (declared 8 August 2026) remains in effect, with active wildfire evacuation orders/alerts listed across the Cariboo Regional District, Regional District of North Okanagan, Okanagan-Similkameen, Thompson-Nicola Regional District, Fraser Valley Regional District and roughly 25 other affected communities; most recent update dated 17 August 2026 (Cariboo Regional District evacuation information).

Re-checked 19 August 2026: EmergencyInfoBC's provincial emergencies listing confirms the State of Provincial Emergency (declared 8 August 2026) remains in effect, with 29 active wildfire evacuation orders/alerts listed, most recently updated 18 August 2026 (Lower Nicola Indian Band and District of Summerland). GDACS's episode 39 update for event WF 1030240 (reporting window 08-17 August 2026) remains the latest available episode, with burned area unchanged at 26,618 hectares and affected population unchanged at 4,912. No newer RCMP release has been found, so the confirmed death toll remains at 1, and no allowlisted source has declared the fires contained.

EmergencyInfoBC, provincial State of Provincial Emergency event page (last updated 8 August 2026, 1:00 pm): 'The Province of British Columbia has declared a State of Provincial Emergency due to regional wildfires,' directing residents to BC Wildfire Service and DriveBC for real-time statistics.

GDACS wildfire report for Canada (event id 1030240, episode 1): 'Forest fire can have a low humanitarian impact based on the burned area and the affected population and their vulnerability.' Burned area: 13,006 hectares. Affected population: 4,746 people in the burned area. Reporting window: 08 Aug 2026 - 11 Aug 2026.

Government of British Columbia news release (10 August 2026, 5:01 pm), 'Supporting Summerland-area evacuees': 'More than 1,000 hotel rooms are available now in the Okanagan for wildfire evacuees,' with nearly 1,000 beds in group lodging throughout the Okanagan, thirteen emergency support services staff and volunteers deployed, a twenty-fold increase in BC Evacuee Helpline staffing capacity, and mobile ServiceBC units deployed to Penticton and Kelowna.

Penticton RCMP statement (9 August 2026): confirms that an 80-year-old Meadow Valley resident 'was attempting to leave her home, along with one member of her family, due to the wildfires when she reportedly died suddenly.' RCMP said they 'believe her death to be a result of the wildfire,' with the BC Coroners Service investigating to confirm the nature of death.

EmergencyInfoBC provincial emergencies listing (checked 12 August 2026, most recent activity dated 11 August 2026): shows an active State of Provincial Emergency and roughly 30 active evacuation-information notices issued by regional districts and First Nations communities, including the Fraser Valley Regional District, Thompson-Nicola Regional District, Central and North Okanagan, Cariboo, and Squamish-Lillooet regions.

GDACS wildfire report for Canada (event id 1030240, episode 22, reporting window 08 Aug 2026 - 12 Aug 2026): 'Forest fire can have a low humanitarian impact based on the burned area and the affected population and their vulnerability.' Burned area: 23,450 hectares (up from 13,006 ha in episode 1). Affected population: 4,911 people in the burned area (up from 4,746).

GDACS wildfire report for Canada (event id 1030240, episode 26, reporting window 08 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC - 13 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC): burned area 24,056 hectares (up from 23,450 ha in episode 22); affected population 4,911 people in the burned area (unchanged from episode 22).

A provincewide state of emergency remains in effect (declared 8 August 2026 by Premier Eby); as of Thursday 13 August 2026, the province had 'more than 1,500 block-booked hotel rooms that are available for evacuees' via renewable weekly Emergency Support Services, after helpline staffing was increased 400% following delays accessing services during peak Summerland-area evacuations.

description: A fast-moving wildfire outbreak swept British Columbia's Interior in early August 2026, led by the Bald Range fire, which was first reported the evening of 7 August 2026 near Summerland in the South Okanagan and grew rapidly overnight, prompting a full evacuation order for the roughly 12,000 residents of the District of Summerland. On 8 August 2026, BC's Minister of Emergency Management and Climate Readiness, Kelly Greene, declared a provincewide State of Provincial Emergency, citing the addition of the fast-moving Bald Range fire and the large-scale overnight evacuation. GDACS assessed the wildfire situation in Canada (event 1030240) as an overall Green alert for low humanitarian impact, recording a burned area of 13,006 hectares and about 4,746 people affected in the burned area for the 8-11 August reporting window -- a snapshot that understates the province-wide response, since it covers only the tracked episode window and GDACS itself flags this as a low-impact rating. The BC government's own emergency-information channels confirm the state of emergency remains active, and the provincial government has begun deploying support resources, including more than 1,000 hotel rooms and nearly 1,000 group-lodging beds in the Okanagan for evacuees, mobile ServiceBC units in Penticton and Kelowna, and a twenty-fold increase in BC Evacuee Helpline staffing capacity. On 9 August 2026, Penticton RCMP confirmed the province's first wildfire-related fatality: an 80-year-old Meadow Valley resident who died suddenly while attempting to evacuate with a family member as the Bald Range fire swept through; RCMP said they believe the death resulted from the wildfire, with the BC Coroners Service investigating to confirm the cause of death. As of the most recent EmergencyInfoBC listing, roughly 30 active evacuation notices remain in effect across multiple regional districts and First Nations communities, including the Fraser Valley, Thompson-Nicola, Central and North Okanagan, Cariboo and Squamish-Lillooet regions. No allowlisted source has declared the state of emergency lifted or the fires contained. GDACS's episode 22 update (12 August 2026) shows the tracked burned area growing to 23,450 hectares and the affected population to 4,911, while EmergencyInfoBC confirms the State of Provincial Emergency remains active; no allowlisted source has declared the fires contained. Re-checked 14 August 2026: GDACS's episode 26 update (reporting window 08-13 August 2026) shows the tracked burned area growing to 24,056 hectares, up from 23,450 ha in episode 22, while the affected population within the burned area is unchanged at 4,911; BC government news releases dated 12 August 2026 confirm the State of Provincial Emergency remains active with expanded evacuee support services, but no allowlisted source has declared the fires contained or published an updated province-wide casualty figure. Re-checked 15 August 2026: GDACS's episode 31 update (event WF 1030240, reporting window 08-14 August 2026) shows the tracked burned area growing to 25,391 ha (up from 24,056 ha in episode 26) and the affected population edging up to 4,912 (from 4,911); rcmp.ca confirms no fatality beyond the 9 August death of an 80-year-old Summerland-area evacuee already on file, and emergencyinfobc.gov.bc.ca confirms the State of Provincial Emergency remains active with evacuation orders still in force as of 14 August 2026. No allowlisted source has declared the fires contained. Re-checked 16 August 2026: the provincewide state of emergency remains in effect, driven primarily by the Bald Range wildfire near Summerland; the province had 1,500+ hotel rooms block-booked for evacuees as of 13 August, and multiple regional districts and First Nations still had active wildfire evacuation orders/alerts as of 15 August. No official province-wide death toll, structure-loss count, or hectares-burned figure has been published on an allowlisted source. Re-checked 17 August 2026: GDACS's episode 37 update (event WF 1030240, reporting window 08-16 August 2026) shows the tracked burned area at 25,829 hectares, up from 25,391 ha in episode 31, with the affected population unchanged at 4,912; EmergencyInfoBC's live evacuation listing, checked 17 August 2026, still shows active wildfire evacuation orders/alerts for the Regional District of North Okanagan, Okanagan Indian Band, Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen, District of Summerland, City of Revelstoke and other regional districts and First Nations, with the most recent notices dated 16 August 2026, and the State of Provincial Emergency remains in effect. No newer RCMP release has been found, so the confirmed death toll remains at 1, and no allowlisted source has declared the fires contained. Re-checked 18 August 2026: GDACS's episode 39 update (event WF 1030240, reporting window 08-17 August 2026) shows the tracked burned area growing to 26,618 hectares, up from 25,829 ha in episode 37, with the affected population unchanged at 4,912; EmergencyInfoBC, checked 18 August 2026, confirms the State of Provincial Emergency remains in effect with active wildfire evacuation orders/alerts still listed for the Cariboo Regional District, Regional District of North Okanagan, Okanagan-Similkameen, Thompson-Nicola Regional District, Fraser Valley Regional District and roughly 25 other affected communities, with the most recent notice update dated 17 August 2026 (Cariboo Regional District). No newer RCMP release has been found, so the confirmed death toll remains at 1, and no allowlisted source has declared the fires contained. Re-checked 19 August 2026: EmergencyInfoBC's provincial emergencies listing confirms the State of Provincial Emergency (declared 8 August 2026) remains in effect, with 29 active wildfire evacuation orders/alerts listed, most recently updated 18 August 2026 (Lower Nicola Indian Band and District of Summerland). GDACS's episode 39 update for event WF 1030240 (reporting window 08-17 August 2026) remains the latest available episode, with burned area unchanged at 26,618 hectares and affected population unchanged at 4,912. No newer RCMP release has been found, so the confirmed death toll remains at 1, and no allowlisted source has declared the fires contained.
